stories.title: Read this before you buy that TV streaming stick
stories.titleZh: 购买电视流媒体棒前，请先看这篇
stories.author: speckx
summaryZh: Security experts have been sounding the alarm for years about the risks of using generic TV boxes that promise unlimited content streaming for a one-time fee, warning that they secretly rent the user’s Internet connection out to strangers. But a groundbreaking new analysis finds these devices also routinely spoof themselves as mobile phones clicking ads on AI-generated websites as part of a sprawling operation that seeks to defraud online merchants and advertising networks. Pedro Falé is a threat researcher with the security firm Bitsight. Falé told KrebsOnSecurity he was able to peer inside a vast and complex ad fraud network by registering an expired domain name that was used to coordinate fake ad clicks across a particularly popular brand of these streaming devices known as H96. An H96 TV streaming device currently advertised for sale on Amazon. Falé said the domain he scooped up was previously used for telemetry, periodically collecting full hardware information and the entire list of installed apps from tens of thousands of H96 streaming sticks plugged into television sets around the globe. But upon inspecting the traffic being funneled to the domain, he discovered nearly all of the TV boxes transmitting data claimed to be mobile phone models from a variety of manufacturers, including Samsung, Vivo, Huawei, and Xiaomi. “We noticed something was wildly wrong,” Falé said. “Multiple devices reporting to this factory Android TV Box backdoor were ‘phones.'” Image: Bitsight. The researcher found all of the devices reported having the same two apps installed, and that those apps were made by a company called Zhejiang Fengwo IoT Technology Ltd, an entity founded in 2019 in mainland China which operates an ad-publishing portfolio under the name Fengwo Group. Further investigation into the Fengwo Group revealed it has registered multiple patents that match the inner workings of these apps. “Bitsight TRACE identified several Hong Kong, Singapore, and single person ‘legal’ shell identities used to collect the monetization and traced the operation back to a mainland China company known as Zhejiang Fengwo IoT Technology Co., Ltd, which operates under the Fengwo Group,” Falé wrote in a report released today about their findings. Falé said an analysis of the apps shows they help to coordinate an ad fraud network that uses these H96 devices as a captive traffic source to click on ads at AI-generated websites operated by the Fengwo Group. Bitsight discovered the websites contain machine-generated news articles and graphics across a range of categories, including finance, health, education, gaming, music and food blogs. But they also found none of those sites displayed ads unless the device visiting the page matched the spoofed mobile profile of these H96 devices. AI DIGITAL HUMANS The domain for the Fengwo Group — fwgcloud[.]com — claims the company is “redefining the boundaries of human-AI interaction,” and that it has created more than 120,000 “AI digital humans” available to rent for everything from emotional companionship to 24/7 customer service and creative design. The homepage for fwgcloud dot com. Falé said the Fengwo Group’s domain shared its SSL certificate data with other domains associated with the apps found on H96 devices, specifically the phone spoofing mechanism. He noted the domain also has an internal wiki platform that directly ties the Fengwo Group to a proprietary implementation of a Google-built visual programming language called Blockly, which was originally designed to help kids learn how to write software. According to Bitsight, the Fengwo Group’s employees use Blockly to build the sham websites, allowing low-skilled operators to drag blocks of code together in their Blockly editor — without any need to understand what the underlying code blocks do or how they work. The Blockly homepage. “An operator can drag blocks together in their Blockly editor, to define each fraud routine, given a task type,” reads Bitsight’s report. “Once the routine is saved, it gets exported as JavaScript and uploaded to the S3 buckets. An operator doesn’t need as much understanding of the underlying technicalities, as it is all set in place for ease of use.” Bitsight even found one of the Fengwo Group app developers mentioning exactly these advantages, noting the developer remarked that “only a small number of highly-skilled developers are needed to build the template execution-unit images,” and that “developers who create execution units from those templates have significantly lower technical requirements, greatly reducing the company’s operating costs.” Falé said if a user’s H96 streaming stick is selected for a specific fraud task, it will be pushed the appropriate Blockly module according to the task desired, which can include silently launching a web browser, visiting websites, browsing pages, managing tabs, and clicking on ads. To ensure the TV boxes masquerading as mobile phones can reliably click on ads displayed via the AI-generated websites, the Fengwo group “fuses three vision and reasoning systems into a single interface,” allowing the bots to correctly identify an ad on the webpage and navigate the site much like a human would, the Bitsight report observed. Examples of ad landing pages linked to the Fengwo Group. Image: Bitsight. TV ON? PROXY. TV OFF? AD FRAUD Bitsight found the H96 devices were either relaying residential proxy traffic or participating in ad fraud, but never both at the same time. In fact, they concluded that when these TV boxes detect an HDMI signal from an attached television — indicating the user intends to stream video content — the box is usually functioning as a residential proxy. When the TV is off, it switches back to waiting for ad fraud jobs. Falé said he believes the TV boxes are set up this way because its ad fraud activities are far more resource intensive and could interfere with the device’s stated purpose — streaming video content over the Internet. Despite repeated warnings from the FBI and security industry leaders about the security and privacy risks of using these streaming devices, major e-commerce providers like Amazon, Best Buy, Newegg and others continue to sell hundreds of different models and brands that bundle unofficial versions of Google’s Android operating system and are frequently marketed (via online influencers) as a way to access a broad array of streaming services and live broadcasts without a subscription. Image: fbi.gov. In addition to enlisting the user’s TV box in ad fraud networks, these off-brand streaming devices almost universally come with residential proxy software pre-installed. This software rents the user’s Internet address out to anonymous paying customers, who run the gamut from aggressive content scraping firms to ticket scalpers and outright cybercriminals. What’s more, because these generic (and generally dirt cheap) TV boxes are all horribly insecure by default and bereft of any kind of authentication, installing one on your home or office network only invites further mischief. In January, the proxy tracking service Synthient documented how multiple botnets had rapidly enslaved millions of TV boxes using a complex interplay of security vulnerabilities in both the residential proxy software and the streaming devices themselves. SHOW ME THE MONEY Bitsight said it tracked approximately 38,000 TV boxes globally phoning home to the expired Fengwo Group domain, and based on that number the report estimates this ad fraud network brings in revenues of close to $50,000 a day (not counting substantial revenue from the residential proxy side of the business). However, Falé emphasized that these estimates are highly conservative and based on telemetry from just one of the Fengwo Group’s core (but older) domains. As for the Fengwo Group’s claim to have 120,000 “digital humans” at their disposal, Bitsight’s report concludes it could be just a clever marketing scheme and/or a way to avoid drawing suspicion to the company’s operations. “Historically, when dealing with proxy services or DDoS, we sometimes see these websites undertake inconspicuous facades, so as not to advertise their DDoS capability or botnet size,” Falé wrote in the report. “This could also be the case here.” If the Fengwo Group truly does have tens of thousands of “AI humans” at its beck and call, it does not appear to have dedicated any of them to fielding inquiries from its own website. KrebsOnSecurity sought comment from the Fengwo Group by emailing the contact address listed on the company’s homepage, but the request bounced back with the reply, “Your message couldn’t be delivered to postmaster@fwgcloud[.]com. Their inbox is full, or it’s getting too much mail right now.” As Bitsight’s analysis shows, when it comes to TV boxes and streaming sticks, it’s best to stick to name brands from reputable manufacturers, and then to be sparing and careful with any apps you choose to install on the device — as many of those can bundle residential proxy software as well. Google says consumers can confirm whether or not a device is built with the official Android TV OS and Play Protect certification by following these instructions. Additionally, Synthient maintains a running list of IoT devices that have been known to ship to consumers with residential proxy software and other malicious apps pre-installed. Careful readers will notice Synthient’s list includes other IoT devices apart from streaming sticks and boxes: As the FBI has warned, residential proxy software has also been found in other popular consumer IoT devices from random brands, particularly digital photo frames.

stories.title: Superlogical
stories.author: yan
summaryZh: We are building the the multiplexer for all work. Building and operating software today spans local machines, remote hosts, sandboxes, services, and production systems. It has many modes of operation: interactively with a human developer, automatically through CI and background processes, and increasingly through agents working in parallel. This work is all related, yet today's tools divide it into separate systems. Interactive tools assume a person at an interface. Automatic work disappears into jobs and logs. And as the work moves to production it lives behind separate systems and controls. AI makes this fragmentation more visible and costly, but it did not create it. System administration, continuous integration, remote development and collaboration have strained the same boundaries for decades. We believe the missing layer is a durable session around the work itself: one that can span applications and environments, provide relevant context by default, expose structured data and actions, preserve history, and be driven by software while remaining visible and controllable by people. What we're building This is our plan to build a multiplexer for all work: 1 Build an incredible multiplexer. 2 Make everything in it composable. 3 Make it safe and operable in production. A multiplexer brings multiple independent streams together through a common interface. For us, that means interactive work, automatic work, and production work would share one well-crafted underlying system instead of living in separate tools. We'll begin with a terminal multiplexer. It keeps multiple terminal blocks organized inside a long-lived session, so you can close the application, reconnect from another device, and pick up exactly where you left off. If you're already familiar with terminal multiplexers, you'll feel right at home, but we're bringing a more modern touch. Sessions can be accessed through the web and native macOS/iOS applications, and sharing a live session with other people is built in from the start. We're also addressing the most common papercuts of existing tools, such as making scrollback, selection, and scrolling all work natively. A terminal multiplexer may sound like a narrow place to start a company. Our vision is much larger, but terminals connect developers, agents, tools, and infrastructure so it is the right foundation for everything that follows. We will build a high-quality terminal multiplexer that remains excellent at that job, even as it grows to support the second and third parts of the plan. We'll have more to say about those later. Who we are We're a team that has spent our entire careers building some of the most widely used developer tooling, infrastructure software, and AI systems. We care deeply about well-crafted software that is beautiful to use, reliable in practice, and designed for others to build on. Mitchell Hashimoto Creator of Ghostty. Co-founded HashiCorp and created Vagrant, Terraform, Vault, and more. Spent more than a decade as CEO and CTO from its earliest days through its IPO. Jack Pearkes VP of Engineering and VP of R&D at HashiCorp, and its very first employee. Helped to create HashiCorp's first products and hired and led the original engineering team. Alasdair Monk Head of Experience at Poolside, VP of Design at Vercel, and a senior design leader at HashiCorp and Heroku. Two decades spent designing and building interfaces for developers. Hector Simpson Designed apps, services, and agentic experiences at Poolside. An interface designer and builder who has shipped developer-first products at Heroku, HashiCorp, Clearbit, and Vercel. Superlogical is funded by: Get on the list for our first release We'll let you know when our beta for the terminal multiplexer is available, and any OSS releases along the way.

我想这就是为什么它是一个活跃的研究领域，而且是一个跨学科的领域，什么是智能？是你练习过无数次的东西吗？是你有目的且高效练习的东西吗？“有目的”地做某事意味着什么，其中涉及多少记忆？如果涉及记忆，其中有多少是相关的？什么是解决问题或智慧？什么是创造力？你的记忆中需要多少多样性才能产生创造力？

我的团队每天在我的公司使用这项技术。我在美国汉普顿经营一家设计/建造公司。我们以 3D 优先的方法开始所有设计项目。使用 Rhino3D 或 Revit 以 3D 形式开始原理图设计。我们使用 Enscape 等可视化插件来渲染模型并传输到 Quest 3 耳机。

因此，当客户进来并感到有冒险精神时，我们将设置耳机，将显示高度设置为他们的实际高度，然后让他们在美丽的新家周围走动。

反应非常强烈。我的客户能够真正了解规模、房间比例、天花板高度和最小的细节。

我们能够对模型进行实时更改（在合理范围内）并提供即时设计反馈。

我已经使用这项技术多年，但我很惊讶它没有被更快地采用 - 不过现在对我们来说有好处！

stories.titleZh: Gemini Robotics 2 赋予机器人全身智能
stories.author: ai2027
summaryZh: Google DeepMind 发布 Gemini Robotics 2，为机器人提供全身智能控制、精细操作和多机器人协作能力。
包含三大模型：VLA 模型控制全身动作、ER 模型负责高层推理与任务规划、On-Device 模型支持端侧快速适配新机器人本体。
已在 Apptronik Apollo 2 等人形机器人上验证，可完成行走、抓取、整理房间等复杂现实任务。
highlightsZh: 首次实现人形机器人全身控制，从脚到手指尖协调运动。
支持 22 自由度灵巧手打结、封袋等精细操作，也兼容平行夹爪。
ER 2 模型可执行长达数分钟、数百步决策的复杂任务序列并自我纠错。
引入多机器人协作，不同类型机器人可联合完成单一机器人无法胜任的工作流。
On-Device 2 模型可在数小时内适配全新机器人本体，支持无网络环境本地运行。

stories.title: Google will expand age checks on Android worldwide till the end of the year
stories.titleZh: 谷歌将于年底前在全球范围内扩大Android平台的年龄验证。
stories.author: dmantis
summaryZh: Posted by Paul Feng, VP of Product Management, Google PlayProviding a safe online experience and protecting users from harm is a top priority at Google Play. We take this responsibility seriously and have been investing continuously to offer baseline protections on our platform while also empowering parents with the tools they need to make decisions for their families. Importantly, we also want to empower Play developers with the capabilities to deliver age-appropriate experiences based on their app's content.

To support this, today, we are taking another big step in our ongoing partnership with parents and developers by announcing the expansion of the Google Play Age Signals API to all Play developers globally. stories.title: Stacked PRs are now live on GitHub
stories.titleZh: 堆叠式 PR 现已在 GitHub 上线。
stories.author: tomzorz
summaryZh: Stacked pull requests break large changes into small, reviewable pull requests. They’re an ordered series of pull requests that each represent focused layers of your change. With stacks, you can independently review and check each pull request, then merge everything together in one click. No more opening a single large pull request that takes forever to review, or splitting work across multiple branches you have to keep manually rebasing.

“We’ve been using GitHub stacked PRs for Next.js for the past few months. It has helped us introduce smaller individual changes while shipping larger features, making it easier to review PRs. – Tim Neutkens, NextJS lead, Vercel”

comments.author: dml2135
comments.textZhHtml:
当定制 PR 堆叠工具成为 Graphite 的主要功能时，我没有看到它的吸引力，现在我仍然没有看到它。

堆叠 PR 很有用，但我还没有遇到仅使用普通 git 操作来完成它的人体工程学问题。我的堆叠工作流程大致为：

- 针对 `main` 打开 `branch-1` 的第一个 PR

- 在等待第一个 PR 的审核期间，如果我需要在 `branch-1` 中进行后续工作，我将 `git checkout -b branch-2`，并针对 `branch-1` 打开草稿 PR

- 如果公开审核要求我进行更改以对 `branch-1` 进行更改，我将`branch-2` 上的 `git merge branch-1` 将它们拉入堆栈

- 合并 `branch-1` 后，我的 `branch-2` 草稿 PR 将自动更新为针对 `main` 打开

- 根据需要进行多少堆叠以及我与审阅者相比领先多少，根据需要重复

我不觉得这一切有什么困难或麻烦。此功能是否提供了一些我错过的功能？

comments.author: matharmin
comments.textZhHtml:
我已经使用了预览版一段时间，我很惊讶地看到他们扩展了预览版并有这么多未解决的问题。

例如，合并整个堆栈在许多情况下完全被破坏：https://github.com/github/gh-stack/discussions/212

您可以逐一合并，但如果您使用挤压和合并，则需要一个如果您需要审核，请重新批准堆栈中的每个 PR。这使您失去了可以说是堆叠 PR 的最大收益。

命令行工具（gh stack）有助于减少手动操作，但您仍然需要非常了解 git rebase 的工作原理，该工具只是帮助跨多个分支实现自动化。例如，如果您的本地分支与远程分支不同步，则仅运行 UI 建议的“gh stack rebase”命令将不起作用，并且工具不会向您指出这一点。

我确实发现堆栈 UI 非常好。与独立 PR 相比，它相当小，但足以显示它们之间的关系。

（我的评论都假设您已经有充分的理由堆叠 PR。此工具只是帮助简化工作流程，它没有提供任何新功能）

comments.author: sameenkarim
comments.textZhHtml:
我们正在针对挤压合并问题推出一系列错误修复。

我们有一个称为 CPRMC（创建拉取请求合并提交）的内部系统，用于评估 PR 是否“准备好”合并。这涵盖了从可合并性（检查合并冲突）到规则评估（确保批准与合并将创建的潜在提交相匹配）等所有内容。

当压缩合并多个 PR 堆栈时，这变得特别困难，因为我们必须计算一系列压缩的提交，然后将它们关联回规则/评论。这对于第一个 PR 来说相对容易，但对于第二个 PR 以后，这会变得更加复杂，因为祖先提交被压缩并且不按原样存在于分支上。我不会讨论多父母情况会变得多么复杂，哈哈。

这是我们需要解决的问题，也是团队的首要任务。我们的数据显示，99% 的堆栈合并成功完成，但我们需要提高得更高。

感谢您成为预览版的早期用户并在我们解决这些问题时与我们合作！

comments.textZhHtml:
您能确保对堆栈有良好的 API 支持吗？

我们使用自定义合并队列，我们希望它能够从堆栈中获取多个 PR一次作为单独的 PR。 最后我检查过你必须登陆一个 PR、重新设置堆栈基础、登陆下一个等等。 与简单地并行测试部分或全部堆栈然后声明它们合并相比，这在 CI 时间（和挂钟时间）方面非常昂贵。 本质上，在队列完成其任务后，机器人需要能够说“挤压合并这 3 个堆叠的 PR”。

comments.author: sameenkarim
comments.textZhHtml:
是的，这是我们的首要任务之一。其一，所有堆栈操作都有一个完全公开的 API 。因此，如果您不想使用 `gh stack` CLI，您可以构建自己的：https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/stacks

对于合并，我们有一个 API，但必须将其移至新的异步方法：https://github.github.io/gh-stack/reference/merge-api/

旧版 API 是完全同步的，并且由于多个 PR 的堆栈通常需要 10 秒以上（我们的全局超时），因此我们必须转向异步。

我们已经有一些人使用它来将堆栈集成到他们的合并队列中。 最重要的是，您可以在一个原子操作中获得多个 PR，然后将多个 PR 的所有提交一次推送到 main。因此，不必为每个重新运行构建/部署，它可以触发包含所有更改的最后一次提交。

comments.author: mattmatheson
comments.textZhHtml:
我们使用的是 GitHub 的 API。在 GitHub 支持之前，我们确实开发过一个版本，但它需要使用我们的凭据直接推送到主分支。大多数客户无法接受这种做法，所以我们最终没有发布该版本，而是等待 GitHub 提供支持。

使用 GitHub API 意味着您仍然可以按照人们期望的方式保留历史记录和提交信息（通过队列合并和直接合并的行为一致），并且它能让用户确保我们的合并队列所合并的唯一代码就是 PR 中的代码。

stories.title: KOReader
stories.author: Cider9986
summaryZh: KOReader is a document viewer for E Ink devices. Supported fileformats include EPUB, PDF, DjVu, XPS, CBT, CBZ, FB2, PDB, TXT, HTML, RTF, CHM, DOC, MOBI and ZIP files. It’s available for Kindle, Kobo, PocketBook, Android and desktop Linux.

comments.author: gejose
comments.textZhHtml:
我真的很喜欢它的存在，但我发现菜单和用户界面相当不直观。我的主要用例是在 Kobo 和 iPhone 之间同步阅读进度。我可以在 Kobo 上使用 KOReader 以及 iPhone 上的 Readest 应用程序[1]（也是开源的）来完成此操作。

最终我决定放弃 KOReader，因为它感觉有点滞后。手势（例如：向左侧向上滑动以增加前灯亮度）也效果不佳。

我最终编写了自己的软件，将 Kobo 的进度同步到 KOReader 同步服务器[2]，我的 Readest 应用程序也连接到该服务器（喜欢与 Kindle 不同，Kobo 是一个相当开放的系统）。您甚至可以对其进行设置，以便可以通过 SSH 访问它[3]。

[1] https://github.com/readest/readest [2] https://github.com/koreader/koreader-sync-server [3] https://www.mobileread.com/forums/showthread.php?t=254214

我越狱了它，启动了 KOReader，就像我有了一个新的电子阅读器一样。可定制性的数量有点妨碍，但一旦设置好，我就不会从一个月到下个月真正考虑它。我也不觉得有必要升级我的原始安装。

comments.author: the_lucifer
comments.textZhHtml:
> 我认为它肯定会以用户友好性换取强大功能和灵活性

据我所知，这是一个与 OSS 软件一样古老的故事。到目前为止，我所见过的具有出色用户体验的 FOSS 软件中唯一的例外是 Blender[1]。由于用户体验不是 Linux 上的一等公民，使用可靠的通用工具来创建出色的用户体验也会使事情变得更加恶化。

我认为糟糕的用户体验和 OSS 的问题是共存的，因为良好的用户体验需要一个极其固执己见的头脑来掌舵，以及一种优先考虑功能并说“不，这并不重要”的文化，而 OSS 通常缺乏这种文化。

[1]: https://www.blender.org/

comments.author: pseudony
comments.textZhHtml:
我不知道这一点。

我认为 Libreoffice 比功能区时代的 Office 更容易导航。

我认为尤其是 Gnome，而且 Kde 比 Windows 拥有更好的设置，它分布在新的和经典的视图（或更多？）中。

我还认为 MacOS finder 比 Windows/KDE/Gnome 的同类产品更糟糕。当你剥离太多，以至于人们必须记住奇怪的组合键才能跳转/导航到特定目录时，你真的走得太远了。

在我看来，移动用户体验（android 和 iphone）比任何桌面系统都要糟糕。没有什么是一致的（在应用程序之间共享数据），没有什么似乎是固定的（每隔几个版本，设置就会在中央设置应用程序中移动）。

我们可以深入争论。让我先说一下——品味绝对是一件事，但版本之间的一致性显然是一件好事，除非你经常处于现有用户群与潜在用户群相形见绌的情况。我们坚持使用软盘图标，不要每次发布时都从桌面更改为 Metro 桌面，再更改为 ios 风格的桌面，等等。最后一点：OSS 软件可能会被误导，但它绝不会试图欺骗用户以实现某些企业目标的成功。它不会恶意地将文件存储在云中，也不会主动使数据导出变得困难，也不会被激励不与竞争对手提供的设备或程序进行互操作。

comments.author: skydhash
comments.textZhHtml:
> 到目前为止，我所见过的具有出色用户体验的 FOSS 软件中唯一的例外是 Blender。

大多数 OSS 软件都偏向高级用户而不是完全的初学者。甚至 Blender 也不是一个很好的可发现性练习。您需要经过培训才能使用它。

Kobo 和 kindle 中的库存软件可以在几分钟内使用，因为它们没有很多功能/选项。如果这就是您所需要的，那完全没问题。就像 Windows 7 的记事本一样。但如果你需要更多的功能，你的愿望是notepad++/vim级别（这确实需要更多的学习），这就是koreader。

comments.author: incanus77
comments.textZhHtml:
> 大多数 OSS 软件都偏向高级用户而不是完全的初学者。甚至 Blender 也不是一个很好的可发现性练习。您需要接受培训才能使用它。

我认为它比这更微妙。我是一个高级用户 - 我在 90 年代编译了我的 Linux 内核，20 年前我编写了自己的 SSH 隧道管理器，我总是摆弄设置等等。

但是，我经常对很多 OSS 软件感到沮丧，因为它期望你像工具的开发人员一样思考，而不是对用户有同理心。对于该工具的开发人员来说，显而易见的事情（我在这里提出了一个希望具有代表性的假设，但是在“主题”下找到字体的变化，因为它是“它看起来”的样子，而在“视图”下找到字体大小，因为，嗯，你看到了它）对于一个在头脑中以相同方式关联字体和字体大小的普通人来说，感觉是令人沮丧和荒谬的。再说一次，一般来说，我在这里进行概括，并没有提及任何特定的软件，而是试图说明我的感受。

当我在 2002 年切换到 Mac 时，这是因为这些事情是有道理的。是的，由于这种固执己见的设计心态，过去和现在都存在挫败感，但我认为好处大于积极之处。不幸的是，苹果浪费了这种文化和技能，现在我经常发现这个平台像 OSS 平台一样令人沮丧，以至于我已经切换回平台之间 50/50 的时间分配。

stories.title: AI's top startups are barely publishing their research
stories.titleZh: 人工智能领域的头部初创企业极少发表研究成果。
stories.author: YeGoblynQueenne

comments.author: ninjahawk1
comments.textZhHtml:
我无法代表其他初创公司发言，但我带着让AI从被动转为主动的想法申请了最新一期的YC，并且在入选前，我已经发表了一篇关于递归自我改进并映射到Epoch AI数据的论文。

我联系了一位英国大学的教授，他回复了我，因为他也在做类似的研究，然后问我想不想和他见个面。我们聊了大约一个小时，因为我们的研究结果有重合，但方法不同，特别是假设不同。

我说这些是想表达，作为一名正在读本科的物理系学生，仅仅通过做独立研究并与专家交流，就能让我结识否则可能永远不会认识的人。对于刚进入任何行业的年轻人来说，做研究是结识新人的绝佳途径。

comments.author: sillysaurusx
comments.textZhHtml:
这也是大型实验室停止公开论文的原因之一。发表论文对那些没有其他途径引起聪明陌生人注意的人来说最有价值。一旦你能雇佣几乎任何人，而且每个人都会回复你的电话，那么发表论文剩下的主要作用就是告诉竞争对手哪些方法奏效了。

这是每个领域从科学转变为产业时都会发生的现象。化学家们曾自由地发表论文，直到染料开始变得值钱，然后有趣的研究就转移到了公司实验室里，不再对外公布了。

comments.author: teleforce
comments.textZhHtml: 这就显得非常讽刺和自私了，尤其是当你们的商业模式主要依赖于基于现有公开数据（包括学术和非学术数据）进行模型训练时。

comments.author: ReactiveJelly
comments.textZhHtml: 这就是为什么我们应该推行著佐权

comments.author: fluoridation
comments.textZhHtml: 这跟那码事毫无关系。如果你发表了一篇著佐权论文，这并不能强迫那些基于你的论文开发产品的人去发表更多论文。

comments.author: fc417fc802
comments.textZhHtml: GNU RPL（研究公共许可证），一种病毒式知识许可证。通过阅读这篇论文，你在法律上有义务公开你进行的所有稍微相关的未来研究。

comments.author: fluoridation
comments.textZhHtml:
顺便说一下，已经有一个RPL了：https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reciprocal_Public_License

你的RPL是无法执行的。版权法不处理人们脑海中闪过的抽象思想。据我所知，即使是GPL也处于某种灰色地带，因为它的传染性特征及其对“衍生作品”的定义从未在法庭上接受过检验。也许在合同法下可以，但我不知道。退一步说，我很想听听最终的裁决。

comments.author: fc417fc802
comments.textZhHtml:
嗯，这是一个笑话，显然很愚蠢，但我相信只要许可方可以终止协议并起诉损害赔偿，它就可以强制执行。如果我可以同意付钱给你，让你不要谈论某件事（即保密协议）或不在某个领域工作（即非竞争条款），那么为什么我不能付钱给你，要求你发布你在特定领域未来所做的所有工作？ （“所有未来的工作”可能过于宽泛；您可能不得不将其限制在几年内，但我不是律师。）

我不认为 GPL 处于灰色地带。当您获得作品许可时，通常会附加各种条件。相反，IIUC 没有人特意测试 GPL，主要是因为它显然在范围内，而且任何违规行为都有可能成为公关灾难，因为违规行为毫不夸张是掠夺公共资源的例子。

comments.author: fluoridation
comments.textZhHtml:
>终止协议

什么意思？从人们的头脑中夺回想法？您可以终止协议，即撤销对论文的访问权限，但您发现违规者可能已经将研究成果用于您发现他们违规的用途。你就像是在马儿逃跑后关上大门。

>起诉损害赔偿

老实说，我不知道你可以因为不发表研究而索赔什么损害赔偿。我认为您需要提前在协议上设定一个价值。

>如果我可以同意支付您不谈论某事（即保密协议）或不在某个领域工作（即非竞争条款）的费用，那么为什么我不能支付您在特定领域发布您未来所做的所有工作的费用？

不知道为什么您在条款中添加了“支付”一词，但无论如何。原因是现有合同有明确的界限。保密协议可阻止您泄露一组非常具体的信息。竞业禁止条款会阻止您在特定领域工作。您的提案的范围尚未明确。什么才算是研究？什么才算“相关”？看来，如果我同意这样一份合同，我的整个生活，无论是私人的还是职业的，在读完这篇论文后都将受到合同的保护，我所做的任何事情都可能受到审查。我从来没有可以下班的时候。 “那是什么？你读了我关于压缩的论文，并且正在研究一个使用压缩的副项目？你一定要看看一些关于它的出版物。”

>相反，IIUC 没有人特意测试 GPL，主要是因为它显然在范围内
